title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). E and K are extensions of Q. A 'CM structure' Sigma is an open-closed ideal of E (x) K whose quotient t = (E (x) K)/Sigma is a 'CM-type bimodule'. It defines a homomorphism of Q-tori Psi_Sigma : T_K -> T_E (with T_F = Res_{F/Q} G_m), given by x |-> det_{t/E}(x). In the language of characteristic functions this is Psi_Sigma(x) = N_{E(x)K/E}(x^{1_Sigma}). The previous page also showed compatibility with norm maps (from finite extensions K'/K) and with inclusions (into extensions E'/E).

On this page:
(1) Because of that compatibility, one may reduce to the minimal pair (E_0, K_0) over which Sigma is defined. So E and K may be assumed finite.
(2) Pass to character groups over Q-bar (or C): X(T_E) = Z^{I_E} and X(T_K) = Z^{I_K}, with I_F = Hom(F, Q-bar). The transposed map Z^{I_E} -> Z^{I_K} is the matrix 1_Sigma, viewed as a 0/1 function on I_E x I_K. Hence knowing Sigma is the same as knowing Psi_Sigma, and Psi_Sigma is not an arbitrary torus map.
(3) Take a Galois closure E-bar, and let K be finite of degree 2d'. Then Sigma amounts to a CM type in the usual sense: a set {sigma_1, ..., sigma_d'} of embeddings K -> E-bar such that the sigma_i together with tau sigma_i (tau = complex conjugation in Gal(E-bar/Q)) exhaust Hom(K, E-bar). So Psi_Sigma(x) = prod_i sigma_i(x). This is the classical type norm of Shimura-Taniyama, landing in (a field containing) the reflex field.
(4) For K a CM field with maximal totally real subfield K_r, the restrictions sigma_i|K_r run once through Hom(K_r, E-bar). Hence Psi_Sigma restricted to T_{K_r} is N_{K_r/Q}, so Psi_Sigma kills V_{K_r}, the norm-one (maximal anisotropic, 'compact') subtorus of T_{K_r}.
(5) That subtorus contains the Zariski closure of a finite-index subgroup of the units of K (unit rank of K equals that of K_r). Combined with an earlier section (the 'f'' reference), this gives a factorization T_K -> S_K^0 -> T_E. Here S_K^0 is the quotient of T_K by the closure of the units: the (connected) Serre group of K.

Next page: Psi_Sigma o i_K = x^{d'} on G_m (weight compatibility), and the question whether the Psi_Sigma, for all CM types on K, form a faithful family on S_K^0. He answers yes by switching one embedding at a time.

Purpose: build the 'CM part' of the motivic Galois group. CM abelian varieties / CM motives give representations of S_K^0 through type norms, i.e. the identification of the Galois group of CM motives with the Serre group.
errors: No substantive mathematical error. Step (4) tacitly assumes K is a CM field (or totally real), so that complex conjugation induces a well-defined involution on K with fixed field K_r. The general 'E, K arbitrary' framework of the previous page needs this reduction, which is only implicit.

Step (5) needs the units of K to be, up to finite index, the units of K_r. It also needs their Zariski closure to lie in (in fact, up to connected component, equal) the norm-one torus of K_r. This is true but not argued on the page; it is deferred to an earlier section ('des f''?').

ideas.what: CM structure as an open-closed ideal of E(x)K, i.e. a monogenic E(x)K-bimodule; type map Psi_Sigma(x) = det_{t/E}(x) = N_{E(x)K/E}(x^{1_Sigma})
ideas.modern_name: CM type and its type norm / reflex-norm torus homomorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura-Taniyama (1961); torus formulation by Serre (1968), Deligne, Milne
ideas.where_published: not in Grothendieck's published texts as far as known

ideas.what: Character-group description: the transpose of Psi_Sigma is the 0/1 matrix 1_Sigma on I_E x I_K, so Sigma is determined by Psi_Sigma
ideas.modern_name: CM types as characters of the Serre group (functions on Hom(K, Q-bar) with f + f o c constant)

ideas.what: Type norm restricted to the totally real subfield equals N_{K_r/Q}; hence it kills the closure of units and factors through T_K -> S_K^0
ideas.modern_name: Factorization of the type norm through the Serre group S^K
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (1968, ch. II); Deligne 'Motifs et groupe de Taniyama' (1982)

ideas.what: Faithfulness of the family {Psi_Sigma} on S_K^0 (next page), with weight relation Psi_Sigma o i_K = x^{d'}
ideas.modern_name: The Serre group is the motivic Galois group of CM motives (CM motives generate its representations)

missed.claim: Historical: if the 1965 dating holds, Grothendieck was here tying CM types to a 'Serre-group' quotient of T_K by the closure of units. That anticipates, within his Galois theory of motives, the identification of the motivic Galois group of CM motives with the Serre group, usually attributed to Serre 1968 and Deligne 1982. The notation S_K^0 may however reflect knowledge of Serre's work, and the file is dated up to ca. 1977, so the priority is uncertain.
missed.quote: on conclut que si K fini sur Q, alors Psi_Sigma: T_K -> T_E se factorise par S K° -> T_E
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's own route to the Serre/Taniyama group as a motivic Galois group. It uses an intrinsic bimodule formulation of CM types (ideals of E(x)K) that is slightly unusual and functorial in both fields.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (type norm, factorization through the Serre group, faithfulness of CM types) is now standard. Interest is historical: Grothendieck's motivic framing and possibly early date. The dating and the overlap with Serre's 1968 work make priority unclear.
transcription_corrections: '(donc E,K réels et finis)' is doubtful; the context suggests '(donc E, K ... et finis)', likely about E, K being finite (possibly 'algébriques' or 'CM'). The word is not 'réels'.
'Dans le concordance de Σ équivaut : celle de Ψ_Σ' should read 'Donc la connaissance de Σ équivaut à celle de Ψ_Σ (cette dernière n'étant d'ailleurs pas quelconque...)'.

'Identifiant les duals de T_E, T_K à des ... Z^{I_E}, Z^{I_K}': the marginal insertion is '(complexifiés : C)' or similar, i.e. the character groups over Q-bar/C. The transposed map goes Z^{I_E} -> Z^{I_K}.
'par la condition définie par T_Σ' is better read as '... défini par Ψ_Σ' (the transposed homomorphism of Ψ_Σ).
Insertion after Galois closure: 'K fini (degré 2d') sur Q'.
'les {τσ_i, σ_i} forment l'ensemble des ± les hom' should read 'les {τσ_i, σ_i} forment l'ensemble de tous les hom K -> Ē'.
'si K est réel' should read 'si K_r est le sous-corps réel [maximal]': the σ_i|K_r are all the homomorphisms K_r -> Ē.
